name: surface-turn
description: A box can be placed by its centre and turned about it. The standing body's left toes are at x 0.15..0.22, y -0.17..-0.13, the lowest (toe3-3.L at (0.1916, -0.1711)) 2 cm up. A box 0.05 m wide and 0.8 m deep with its centre at (0.5, -0.15) and its top at 0.3 m spans x 0.475..0.525, y -0.55..0.25: no foot is over it, so the physics pass lifts nothing. Turned 90 degrees about its centre it spans x 0.1..0.9, y -0.175..-0.125 (its stored corners stay as they were; `turn` says 90): the left toes are now over it, 28 cm under its top, so the one frame is lifted (28 cm, onto the box). Only the left toes then carry the body (the right foot hangs 28 cm over the floor) and the centre of mass, over the middle, is outside them, so the frame is balanced too (the hips move over the left toes). The keyed root offset stays (0, 0, 0.9450102).
